correctness.rationale: The decomposition of unit prime powers into p−1 Teichmuller cosets mod p² and the nonunit branch into p^p-scaled Haar images yields an exact convolution-of-probability-measures identity. Its residual mass falls as p^(−2k), ruling out any atom; finite quotient normalization gives every asserted R formula. Square averaging gives exact cross term 2(p−1)/p² and multiplier p^(p−4). Valuation shells produce matching upper and lower geometric-series tests, proving the sharp s=p/(p−2) boundary, with almost-sure/Ls convergence by conditional expectation. A separately written exact integer checker confirms 23,793 complete target residues and corresponding rational second moments for p=5,7,11. These experiments are not used to infer infinite assertions.

value.rationale: The output is a natural arithmetic probability law at primes dividing the exponent, where all derivatives vanish modulo p and nonsingular Hensel lifting fails. It determines every finite prime-power multiplicity, the four-variable collision energy at all depths, divergence growth and sharp integrability across an infinite family; finite Teichmuller additive coincidences control actual arithmetic phenomena, rather than an arbitrary census. The exact p=5 formula gives a concrete nontrivial instance and documents applicability.
